Resource Access Protocols

Four necessary conditions for a deadlock:

  1. Mutual Exclusion: Only one task can use a specific resource at a time (it is non-shareable).
  1. Hold and Wait: A task is holding a resource it already has while waiting to get another one.
  1. No Preemption: A resource cannot be forcibly taken from a task, the task must release it voluntarily.
  1. Circular Wait: A closed chain of tasks exists where each task is waiting for a resource held by the next task in the chain.

A resource is any software structure that can be used by a process to advance its execution

  • can be private or shared
    • A shared resource protected against concurrent accesses is called an exclusive resource

To ensure consistency of the data structures in exclusive resources, any concurrent operating system should use appropriate resource access protocols to guarantee a mutual exclusion among competing tasks

  • A piece of code executed under mutual exclusion constraints is called a critical section
  • A task waiting for an exclusive resource is said to be blocked on that resource
  • A semaphore is a kernel data structure that, apart from initialization, can be accessed only through two kernel primitives, usually called wait and signal
    • For each resource RkR_kRk​﻿ I have a binary semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿
    • Each critical section that uses RkR_kRk​﻿ must start with wait(R_k) and finishes with signal(R_k)
    • All tasks blocked on a resource are kept in a queue associated with the semaphore that protects the resource

For classical semaphores I have these rules:

  1. Access Rule (Decides whether to block and when)
    • enter a critical section if the resource is free, block if the resource is locked
  1. Progress Rule (Decides how to execute in a critical section)
    • execute the critical section with the nominal priority
  1. Release Rule (Decides how to order pending requests)
    • Wake up the blocked task with the highest priority
    • Wake up the blocked task in FIFO order

Priority Inversion Problem in case of preemption:

  • In general, the duration of the blocking time of τ1τ_1τ1​﻿ is unbounded, since any intermediate-priority task that can preempt τ3τ_3τ3​﻿ will indirectly block τ1τ_1τ1​﻿

Notation and Assumptions

There is a a set of n periodic tasks, τ1,τ2,...,τnτ_1, τ_2, . . . , τ_nτ1​,τ2​,...,τn​﻿, which cooperate through m shared resources, R1,R2,...,RmR_1,R_2, . . .,R_mR1​,R2​,...,Rm​﻿

We use two distinct priority per task:

  1. Fixed nominal priority PiP_iPi​﻿ assigned for example with RM algorithm
    • Assume that the tasks are ordered by decreasing nominal priority (all tasks have different PiP_iPi​﻿)
    • Tasks with same priority are executed by the FCFS (first come first served)
  1. Dynamic active priority pi≥Pip_i \ge P_ipi​≥Pi​﻿, that is initialized to PiP_iPi​﻿
  • Tasks do not suspend them selves on I/O operations or on explicit synchronization
    primitives (except on locked semaphores)
  • A task will release all of its locks, if it holds any, before or at the end of its execution

Critical sections could be nested only in this way:

Algorithms

Non-Preemptive Protocol (NPP)

Remove preemption whenever entering a critical section

  • This can be done by raising the priority to the maximal level pi(Rk)=max⁡hPhp_i(R_k) = \max_h P_hpi​(Rk​)=maxh​Ph​﻿ and reset to pi=Pip_i = P_i pi​=Pi​﻿ when leaving

NPP is appropriate when tasks use short critical sections because it can creates unnecessary blocking (τ1τ_1τ1​﻿)

The protocol can be implemented by changing the behavior of the wait and signal primitives

  • wait(s): pi = max(P1, …, Pn)
  • signal(s): pi = Pi

Advantages:

  1. No task ever waits for a semaphore, since surely is executing the one with the resource
    • No semaphores queues
  1. Each high-priority task, wait at most one lower priority one
  1. I cannot have deadlocks since I cannot have circular waits, since I cannot be preempted
  1. It is transparent to the programmer

General definitions:

  • BiB_iBi​﻿ denotes the maximum blocking time task τiτ_iτi​﻿ can experience
  • zi,kz_{i, k}zi,k​﻿ denotes a generic critical section of task τi\tau_iτi​﻿ guarded by a semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿
  • Zi,kZ_{i, k}Zi,k​﻿ denotes the longest critical section of task τi\tau_iτi​﻿ guarded by a semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿
    • δi,k\delta_{i, k} δi,k​﻿ denotes the duration of Zi,kZ_{i, k}Zi,k​﻿
  • γi\gamma_iγi​﻿ denotes the set of all the longest critical sections that can block τi\tau_iτi​﻿

A process is blocked when is waiting for the CPU due to a process with a lower nominal priority

  • When a process is waiting for the CPU due to a higher priority process, the process is ready and not blocked
  • if there aren’t shared resources, than I do not have blocking time
  • if there are shared resources and preemption a task could be blocked by a lower priority ones

Blocking Time Computation in NPP:

  1. γi={Zj,k∣Pj<Pi,k=1,...,m}\gamma_i = \{ Z_{j, k} | P_j < P_i, k=1, ..., m \}γi​={Zj,k​∣Pj​<Pi​,k=1,...,m}﻿ → since τi\tau_iτi​﻿ cannot preempt a lower priority task τj\tau_jτj​﻿ in critical section
  1. Since τi\tau_iτi​﻿ can be blocked only one task with lower priority: Bi=max⁡j,k{δj,k−1∣Zj,k∈γi}B_i = \max_{j, k} \{ \delta_{j, k} - 1 | Z_{j, k} \in \gamma_i \}Bi​=maxj,k​{δj,k​−1∣Zj,k​∈γi​}﻿
    • A time unit is subtraced since Zj,kZ_{j,k} Zj,k​﻿ must start before the arrival of τi\tau_iτi​﻿ in order to block it

Higest Locker Priority Protocol (HLPP)

It raises the priority of a task that uses RkR_kRk​﻿ to the highest priority among the tasks that shares RkR_kRk​﻿

  • pi(Rk)=max⁡h{Ph∣τh uses Rk}p_i(R_k) = \max_h \{ P_h | \tau_h \text{ uses } R_k \}pi​(Rk​)=maxh​{Ph​∣τh​ uses Rk​}﻿ and resetted to PiP_iPi​﻿ at exit (the previous one since I could have nested critical sections)
  • I can compute the priority ceiling (C(Rk)=max⁡h{Ph∣τh uses Rk}C(R_k) = \max_h \{ P_h | \tau_h \text{ uses } R_k \}C(Rk​)=maxh​{Ph​∣τh​ uses Rk​}﻿) off-line
    • this algorithm is called also Immediate Priority Ceiling

Blocking time computation:

  • γi={Zj,k∣Pj<Pi∧C(Rk)≥Pi,   k=1,...,m}\gamma_i = \{ Z_{j, k} | P_j < P_i \land C(R_k) \ge P_i, \ \ \ k=1, ..., m \}γi​={Zj,k​∣Pj​<Pi​∧C(Rk​)≥Pi​,   k=1,...,m}﻿

Theorem: Under HLP, a task τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked, at most, for the duration of a single critical section belonging to the set γiγ_iγi​﻿

  • Bi=max⁡j,k{δj,k−1∣Zj,k∈γi}B_i = \max_{j, k} \{ \delta_{j, k} - 1 | Z_{j, k} \in \gamma_i \}Bi​=maxj,k​{δj,k​−1∣Zj,k​∈γi​}﻿

Proof:

Let assume that τi\tau_iτi​﻿ can be blocked by two critical sections zi,az_{i, a}zi,a​﻿ and zi,bz_{i, b}zi,b​﻿

  • both must belong to different tasks τ1\tau_1τ1​﻿ and τ2\tau_2τ2​﻿ with priorities lower then PiP_iPi​﻿
  • Both must have a ceiling higher than PiP_i Pi​﻿ → P1<Pi≤C(Ra)P_1 < P_i \le C(R_a)P1​<Pi​≤C(Ra​)﻿ and P2<Pi≤C(Rb)P_2 < P_i \le C(R_b)P2​<Pi​≤C(Rb​)﻿

τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked twice only if τ1τ_1τ1​﻿ and τ2τ_2τ2​﻿ are both inside the resources when τiτ_iτi​﻿ arrives, and this can occur only if one of them (say τ1τ_1τ1​﻿) preempted the other inside the critical section

  • But, if τ1τ_1τ1​﻿ preempted τ2τ_2τ2​﻿ inside z2,bz_{2,b}z2,b​﻿ it means that P1>C(Rb)P_1 > C(R_b)P1​>C(Rb​)﻿, which is a contradiction

The protocol can be implemented by changing the behavior of the wait and signal primitives:

  • wait(S): pi = max{pi, C(S)}
  • signal(S): pi = prev pi → that is PiP_iPi​﻿ or in case of nested CS the previous pip_ipi​﻿

Advantages:

  • Semaphores queues are not needed, because tasks never block on a wait
  • No deadlocks can happen

Problems:

  • blocking could be unnecessary (same pessimism as for NPP)
    • In fact, a task is blocked at the time it attempts to preempt, before it actually requires a resource
    • Such a source of pessimism is removed in PIP by postponing the blocking condition at the entrance of a critical section rather than at the activation time
    • If a critical section is contained only in one branch of a conditional statement, then the task could be unnecessarily blocked
  • It is not transparent to the programmer (due to ceilings that need to be computed)

Priority Inheritance Protocol (PIP)

When a task τiτ_iτi​﻿ blocks one or more higher-priority tasks, it temporarily assumes (inherits) the highest active priority of the blocked tasks

  • It solves the NPP and HLPP pessimism, since it blocks τ1\tau_1τ1​﻿ only if it access the resource

At every instant: pj(Rk)=max⁡{Pj,max⁡h{ph∣τh is currently blocked on Rk}}p_j(R_k)=\max \{P_j, \max_ h \{p_h|τ_h \ \text{is currently blocked on } R_k\}\}pj​(Rk​)=max{Pj​,maxh​{ph​∣τh​ is currently blocked on Rk​}}﻿

When τj\tau_jτj​﻿ exits the CS, pjp_jpj​﻿ is updated as follow:

  • if no other tasks are blocked by τjτ_jτj​﻿, pjp_jpj​﻿ is set to its nominal priority PjP_jPj​﻿
  • otherwise it is set to the highest priority of the tasks blocked by τjτ_jτj​﻿

Priority inheritance is transitive

  • if a task τ3τ_3τ3​﻿ blocks a task τ2τ_2τ2​﻿, and τ2τ_2τ2​﻿ blocks a task τ1τ_1τ1​﻿, then τ3τ_3τ3​﻿ inherits the priority of τ1τ_1τ1​﻿ via τ2τ_2τ2​﻿, even with different resources blocked

A high-priority task can experience two kinds of blocking:

  • Direct blocking occurs when a higher-priority task tries to acquire a resource already held by a lower-priority task
    • Direct blocking is necessary to ensure the consistency of the shared resources
  • Push-through blocking occurs when a medium-priority task is blocked by a low-priority task that has inherited a higher priority from a task it directly blocks
    • Push-through blocking is necessary to avoid unbounded priority inversion

Protocol Properties

Lemma 1 A semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿ can cause push-through blocking to task τiτ_iτi​﻿, only if SkS_kSk​﻿ is accessed both by a task with priority lower than PiP_iPi​﻿ and by a task with priority higher than PiP_iPi​﻿

Proof Lemma 1: Suppose that semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿ is accessed by a task τlτ_lτl​﻿ with priority lower than PiP_iPi​﻿, but
not by a task with priority higher than PiP_iPi​﻿. Then, τlτ_lτl​﻿ cannot inherit a priority higher than PiP_iPi​﻿. Hence, τlτ_lτl​﻿
will be preempted by τiτ_iτi​﻿ and the lemma follows

Lemma 2 Transitive priority inheritance can occur only in the presence of nested critical sections.

Proof A transitive inheritance occurs when a high-priority task τHτ_HτH​﻿ is blocked by a medium-priority task τMτ_MτM​﻿, which in turn is blocked by a low-priority task τLτ_LτL​﻿.

  • Since τHτ_HτH​﻿ is blocked by τMτ_MτM​﻿, τMτ_MτM​﻿ must hold a semaphore, say SaS_aSa​﻿. But τMτ_MτM​﻿ is also blocked by τLτ_LτL​﻿ on a different semaphore, say SbS_bSb​﻿. This means that τMτ_MτM​﻿ attempted to lock SbS_bSb​﻿ inside the critical section guarded by SaS_aSa​﻿. The lemma follows

Consequences of Lemma 2: if there are no nested critical section, there is no transitive priority inheritance

  • Important since if no transitivity I can discard transitivity blocking in the computation of blocking time

Lemma 3: If there are lil_ili​﻿ lower-priority tasks that can block a task τiτ_iτi​﻿, then τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked for at most the duration of lil_ili​﻿ critical sections (one for each of the lil_ili​﻿ lower priority tasks), regardless of the number of semaphores used by τiτ_iτi​﻿.

Proof:

  • βi,jβ_{i,j}βi,j​﻿ is the set of all critical sections of the lower priority task τjτ_jτj​﻿ which can block τiτ_iτi​﻿ (if there is at least one critical section of τj\tau_jτj​﻿ that uses a semaphore also used by τi\tau_iτi​﻿)
  • Zj,kZ_{j,k}Zj,k​﻿ is a critical section of task τiτ_iτi​﻿ guarded by semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿
  • A lower-priority task τjτ_jτj​﻿ can block a task τiτ_iτi​﻿ only if τjτ_jτj​﻿ is executing within a critical section Zj,k∈βi,jZ_{j,k} ∈ β_{i,j}Zj,k​∈βi,j​﻿ (that can block τiτ_iτi​﻿) when τiτ_iτi​﻿ is initiated
  • If τj∈βi,jτ_j \inβ_{i,j}τj​∈βi,j​﻿ then Pj≥PiP_j\ge P_iPj​≥Pi​﻿ due to direct block or priority inheritance
  • Once τjτ_jτj​﻿ exits Zj,kZ_{j,k}Zj,k​﻿, it can be preempted by τiτ_iτi​﻿; thus, τiτ_iτi​﻿ cannot be blocked by τjτ_jτj​﻿ again.
  • The same situation may happen for each of the lil_ili​﻿ lower-priority tasks, therefore, τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked at most lil_ili​﻿ times

Lemma 4 If there are sis_isi​﻿ distinct semaphores that can block a task τiτ_iτi​﻿, then τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked for at most the duration of sis_isi​﻿ critical sections, regardless of the number of critical sections used by τiτ_iτi​﻿

Proof: Since semaphores are binary, only one of the lower-priority tasks, say τj\tau_jτj​﻿, can be within a blocking critical section corresponding to a particular semaphore SkS_kSk​﻿

  • Once SkS_kSk​﻿ is unlocked, τjτ_jτj​﻿ can be preempted and no longer block τiτ_iτi​﻿
  • If all sis_isi​﻿ semaphores that can block τiτ_iτi​﻿ are locked by sis_isi​﻿ lower-priority tasks, then τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked at most si times

Theorem 1: Under the PIP, a task τiτ_iτi​﻿ can be blocked for at most the duration of αi=min⁡(li,si)α_i = \min(l_i, s_i)αi​=min(li​,si​)﻿ critical sections, where lil_ili​﻿ is the number of lower-priority tasks that can block τiτ_iτi​﻿ and sis_isi​﻿ is the number of distinct semaphores that can block τiτ_iτi​﻿

Proof: follows directly by lemma 3 and 4

PIP Problems

  1. It doesn’t prevent deadlocks
  1. Chained Blocking: athough PIP bounds the priority inversion phenomenon, the blocking duration for a task can still be substantial

Advantages:

  1. No pessimism of NPP and HLP
  1. Transparent to the programmer

Schedulability Tests for Periodic Γ\GammaΓ﻿ with Resource Constraints

Typically the algorithms seen for resource access protocols are used with static priority scheduling algorithm. The schedulability tests presented for periodic task can be extended to include blocking terms BiB_iBi​﻿

  • In general, all the extended tests guarantee one task τiτ_iτi​﻿ at the time, by inflating its computation time CiC_iCi​﻿ by the blocking factor BiB_iBi​﻿
  • All the guarantee tests that were necessary and sufficient under preemptive scheduling become only sufficient since the blocking times are worst-case scenarios

RM Tests

Γ\GammaΓ﻿ is schedulable by RM with critical sections (fixed priorities and Ti=DiT_i = D_iTi​=Di​﻿) if:

  • ∀i≤n,∑k=1i−1CkTk+Ci+BiTi≤i(21/i−1)\forall i \le n, \quad \sum_{k=1}^{i-1} \frac{C_k}{T_k} + \frac{C_i + B_i}{T_i} \le i(2^{1/i} - 1) ∀i≤n,∑k=1i−1​Tk​Ck​​+Ti​Ci​+Bi​​≤i(21/i−1)﻿
  • Or usign the Hyperbolic Test: ∀i≤n,[∏k=1i−1(CkTk+1)](Ci+BiTi+1)≤2\forall i \le n, \quad \left[\prod_{k=1}^{i-1} \left(\frac{C_k}{T_k} + 1\right) \right] \left(\frac{C_i + B_i}{T_i} + 1\right) \le 2 ∀i≤n,[∏k=1i−1​(Tk​Ck​​+1)](Ti​Ci​+Bi​​+1)≤2﻿
